channel.description: Latest articles from Hartford Business Journal (hartfordbusiness.com)

item.title: 🔒 Policyholders seek to intervene in PHL Variable rehabilitation, allege ‘secret backroom negotiations’
item.description: Two large policyholders are demanding financial disclosures and relief from premium payments as the state moves toward liquidating a Hartford-based insurer after rehabilitation efforts collapsed.

item.title: 🔒 Edgewell sells feminine care business for $340M amid restructuring that includes Milford plant closure
item.description: Shelton-based Edgewell Personal Care Co. has sold its feminine care business to Swedish hygiene products company Essity AB for $340 million, advancing a broader restructuring aimed at streamlining operations and […]

item.title: 🔒 As CT legislators convene for 2026 session, bills target business affordability
item.description: There are 107 bills — 82 in the Senate, 25 in the House — already proposed by legislators as the state General Assembly convenes its 2026 session on Wednesday.

item.title: Five UConn Business School alumni, including former basketball star, to join hall of fame
item.description: The UConn School of Business will induct five alumni into its Hall of Fame on April 24, including former NBA player Emeka Okafor and executives from aerospace, health care and real estate sectors.

item.title: 🔒 FuelCell Energy finalizes separation agreement with former general counsel
item.description: FuelCell Energy Inc. will pay former Executive Vice President and General Counsel Joshua Dolger nearly $400,000 in severance under a separation agreement finalized this week, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

item.title: 🔒 Stanley Black & Decker continues to pivot manufacturing out of China to counter tariffs
item.description: The company says it has also raised prices to counter tariffs, inflation and higher raw material costs.

item.title: 🔒 Nutmeg State Financial Credit Union to move Hamden branch after merger
item.description: CrossPoint Federal Credit Union’s former headquarters branch in Hamden is slated to relocate following its merger with the much larger Nutmeg State Financial Credit Union.

item.title: 🔒 With industrial properties ‘in huge demand,’ Norwalk warehouse sells for $1.88M

item.title: Santander’s $12.3B Webster deal would reverse years of CT branch closings
item.description: After years of reducing branches in Connecticut, Banco Santander’s $12.3 billion purchase of Webster Financial would give it one of the largest footprints in the state.

item.title: Lamont’s budget: A big rebate; most of the rest stays the course
